answer: Copying the same citations across 134 aliases thus pays the authoring cost 134 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the ledge index resolves every citation against the ridge checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the signal audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. That is 37 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
